ideas: What it is and when you got it
How you use it during a normal day
What life would be like without it

phrases.meaning: keep your attention on one thing

model: The piece of technology I use every day is a pair of wireless noise-cancelling headphones. I bought them about a year and a half ago, when I started working in an open-plan office with around sixty people. The office was always noisy, with phones ringing and people chatting, and I found it really hard to stay focused. A colleague recommended a particular model, so I tried a pair in a shop and bought them the same day. They weren't cheap, but I saw them as an investment. Honestly, they were a game changer. I use them at least five hours a day. In the morning I listen to a podcast on the bus, at work I play quiet background music while I'm writing reports, and in the evening I use them for English listening practice. The battery life is amazing; I only charge them once a week. They're also very user-friendly. There's a small button on the side that switches between modes, so I can hear an announcement at the station without taking them off. The only time I didn't have them was last month, when I left them at a friend's house for three days. I realised how much I can't do without them, because I was tired and distracted all the time. So I'd say they're the most useful thing I've ever bought.
